sources.note: Not this language: p.1 'The Yambasa Language (nugunu...)', informant from Bokito = Nugunu [yas] (nugu1242). Glottolog lists it under yang1293 in error. Only p.1 read (scan, no text layer); not scanned further since irrelevant.

sources.citation: Bebine (Bébiné), Adriel Josias. 2019. Description phonologique et morphosyntaxique du nuasúɛ (langue bantu A62A). Thèse de doctorat, Université de Yaoundé I. 611 pp. HAL tel-03866872 (= Glottolog's 'Bébiné 2018' grammar).
sources.note: Nothing on word stress/accent placement. Ch.1 phonology pp.26-70: sec.1.4 'Les tons' pp.53-61 gives nine surface pitches, three distinctive tones /H, B, BH/ (p.56) reduced to two base tonemes H and L (1.4.4, p.60). Sec.2.2 pp.71-72 defines the phonological word by vowel-harmony domain and pre-pausal demarcative processes (high-vowel devoicing, H lowering), minimally disyllabic; 'unité accentuelle' (p.121-122) used only as synonym of 'mot phonologique' via Dubois' clitic definition.

sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee. 2015. The phonological systems of the Mbam languages of Cameroon with a focus on vowels and vowel harmony. PhD Leiden, LOT Dissertation Series 410.
sources.note: Sec. 2.8 Yangben phonological overview pp.159-181; 2.8.5 Tone p.180: 'Yangben has a two-tone system underlyingly, high and low.' Noun melodies L/H/LH/HL, verb melodies L/HL/H with H spread and downstep. No stress/accent statement anywhere in the book.

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2003. 'Abstract' vowel harmony in Kàlòŋ: a system-driven account. In Sauzet & Zribi-Hertz (eds), Typologie des langues d'Afrique et universaux de la grammaire, vol. 1, 85-112. Paris: L'Harmattan.
sources.note: Vowel-harmony paper on Kàlòŋ = Yangben; marks H/L tone; says nothing about stress or accent.
